messages:
Maria H: hey, anyone else hit a weird redwoodctl login failure after installing from the install.sh on an offline laptop?
Maria H: repro steps: fresh macbook, ran curl | sh installer (air-gapped except for device auth), then tried `redwoodctl local-serve --profile work` and it immediately fails auth with TLS cert verify error. stack: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`.
AJ: hmm, send the exact error output?
Maria H: pasted below: 
```
> $ redwoodctl login --profile work --method device
Error: failed to exchange token: Post "https://auth.redwood-inference.internal/oauth/device": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
Sasha P: That sounds like the config merge step wrote an internal endpoint into the profile when the install script couldn't reach the public control plane and fell back to a cached internal host. awkward.
Kai L: oof. Are you sure the installer didn't pick up a kubecontext/hosts entry from an old dotfiles import?
Maria H: clean user, no dotfiles, but the installer printed this during install: `Using cached control plane endpoint: https://auth.redwood-inference.internal`. I ignored it at the time.
AJ: Can you show `~/.redwood/config.yaml` (redact tokens)?
Maria H: excerpt: 
```
profiles:
  work:
    endpoint: https://auth.redwood-inference.internal
    last_used: 2067889000
```
Sasha P: yep that's the problem. installer has a bug where if it can't finish discovery it merges a saved local endpoint. We used that flow for fast CI images but it shouldn't be default for interactive installs.
DevEx Bot: new issue created: DEVEX-1428 "installer: avoid merging internal cached endpoints on interactive install" (priority=P2) :ticket: 
AJ: Workaround: manually change the profile endpoint to the public hosted endpoint or run `redwoodctl config merge --force --from /usr/local/share/redwood/dist/config.example.yaml` then `redwoodctl login`.
Maria H: tried that, but on the offline laptop the CA chain still fails because it's trying to talk to the internal host on the corp VPN which we don't have. I need a graceful failover to device auth via hosted endpoint.
Kai L: try `REDWOODCTL_LOCAL_FALLBACK=1 redwoodctl login --method device --profile work --endpoint https://auth.redwood.ai` — we added that env var for dev machines. It forces explicit endpoint override.
Maria H: setting env helped. login succeeded with device code flow. thanks.
Sasha P: we should teach the installer to prefer public endpoints for interactive installs and only preserve cached internal endpoints if user passes `--preserve-endpoints`. I can take a PR.
AJ: Also add a clearer message in the installer: "installer couldn't reach discovery; using cached endpoint X — run with --public to force hosted". small UX win.
Maria H: filing a short blurb for the onboarding doc too. folks might hit this during workshops where network is restricted.
DevEx Bot: PR created by Sasha P: github.com/redwood-inference/installer/pull/512 (link) :eyes: 
Kai L: for local testing note: `redwoodctl local-serve --profile work --trust-ca /path/to/corp.pem` will let the CLI accept a corp CA if you have it. saves users from setting system-level certs.
Maria H: adding that to the onboarding notes. thanks all :heart: 
AJ: leaving a small test in e2e: simulate unreachable discovery and ensure installer exits with a clear actionable error unless `--preserve-endpoints` passed.
Sasha P: I'll add the test and the PR message. ETA tomorrow.
Maria H: confirmed fixed locally with env override and the config merge cleanup. closing my loop. :)
